Adjusted assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Credit supply/demand: The July 2021 SLOOS shows broad strengthening in credit demand for C&I loans across small, middle‑market, and large firms, alongside higher borrower inquiries. Banks reported easing terms for C&I loans and easing standards across consumer credit (credit card, auto, and other consumer loans). Foreign banks also reported stronger C&I demand tied to inventory, receivables, capex, and M&A. This signals supportive credit conditions and momentum in real activity.
- Policy stance and outlook: The FOMC remains highly accommodative (ELB, ongoing QE) but signaled tapering “soon,” consistent with substantial further progress. Elevated inflation is characterized as largely transitory, and the outlook still depends on virus dynamics.
- Financial stability context: While accommodative conditions and easier bank lending support growth, they also interact with elevated asset valuations and some leverage/vulnerabilities noted in broader stability discussions; vigilance remains warranted.

Net tone: Stronger loan demand and easier standards from SLOOS tilt the outlook modestly more constructive than an FSR‑only lens, reinforcing the Fed’s confidence in tapering progress while acknowledging residual risks.
